title: Noddy
research: Willughby and Holme describe different scoring. This edition follows the Willughby-based two-player reconstruction.

rulebook.setup: Cut for low dealer. Deal three per person and turn one starter. Ace is 1, faces 10. If the starter is a jack, give the non-dealer two points. Keep a score sheet to 31.
rulebook.turns: First, starting with non-dealer, count scoring combinations in each hand with the starter, including 15s, 25s, 31s, sets, runs and flushes. Then alternate playing cards, calling the total and scoring newly formed combinations with the immediately preceding cards. If you cannot play under or at 31, say go and let the opponent continue.
rulebook.finish: Peg one for the last play, or two for the play reaching 31 exactly. Unplayed cards are dropped at the end of that sequence. Deal again with the other dealer until one reaches 31 points. Use the linked scoring table for exact combination values.
rulebook.teach: Give the group a four-card sample. List all combinations making 15 or 25, then compare the scores with Cribbage.

title: Laugh and Lie Down
research: Table directions below use a simple point system and omit the historical rules for claiming missed opportunities. The linked edition records the original scoring and extra claims.

rulebook.setup: Deal eight per player. Put the remaining twelve cards face up in the center. At the start a player may save a pair from three of one rank or all four of a rank held in hand.
rulebook.turns: Play one card to capture one or three cards of its rank. You may also use two matching cards to capture two of that rank. Save the cards captured together with those you played. A player with no capture adds the rest of their hand face up to the table and stops taking turns.
rulebook.finish: When only one player has cards left, give that player’s remaining hand and the center cards to the dealer for scoring. In this teaching variant each captured pair counts one point, with two bonus points for the last player still holding cards. Rotate dealers and compare totals after five hands.
rulebook.teach: Lay out two matches. Ask which move preserves more possible captures for a later turn. Treat laying down as a normal part of play.

title: Karnöffel
deck: 48 cards, no aces in the French-suited reconstruction

sources.label: David Parlett after van Leyden and Dummett

research: The record includes a 1426 attestation and surviving relatives. The linked reconstruction translates Swiss suit and court symbols and gives the full power table and bidding rules. The classroom version uses a fixed round value.

rulebook.setup: Remove aces and form two opposing sides. Deal one face up to each player, then four more face down. The suit of the lowest first card is elected. On a tie among low cards, use the one dealt first.
rulebook.turns: The player left of the dealer leads. Follow any suit you choose. The highest eligible card wins and leads next. Use the source’s power table: elected jack beats everything; elected six and two beat plain ranks; elected three, four and five have limited powers. Elected seven loses unless led, when only the elected jack beats it. The seven cannot lead the opening trick.
rulebook.finish: First side to three tricks wins a point in the teaching edition. Rotate dealer and play to an agreed point total. The source also describes bidding and scoring for the historical reconstruction.
rulebook.teach: Read the elected-card table together and compare it with an ordinary follow-suit trump game.

title: Leaf Table

sources.label: Historical inspiration: Andrew Lo’s Game of Leaves inquiry

research: New teaching game inspired by the surviving name Game of Leaves. The rules below are a modern invention.

rulebook.setup: Use Ace–10. Deal three face up to each player and put six face-up cards in the center. Draw piles begin with all remaining cards.
rulebook.turns: Choose one of your cards and pair it with a center card. The pair must total 10 or 11. Keep both when your move is legal. Refill the center and your three-card row from the stock if possible. If you have no pair, you may exchange one hand card with a center card and end your turn.
rulebook.finish: End after a full circuit without a capture, even if cards remain in the stock. Score one for a pair totaling 10 and two for a pair totaling 11.
rulebook.teach: Compare making 10 with making 11. Ask the learner to identify what evidence would be needed to call a modern game a historical reconstruction.
